newsitem.title: GERMANY: Villeroy profits tumble on weak consumer demand.
newsitem.headline: Villeroy profits tumble on weak consumer demand.

text.p: German tableware and bathroom fixtures manufacturer Villeroy & Boch, struggling with weak consumer demand, said on Monday profits slumped 88 percent to 5.1 million marks ($3.4 million) in the first half of 1996.

The group said its "disappointing results" were shaped mainly by a sharp and unexpected 15.4 percent drop in sales of luxury bathroom fittings as customers preferred less expensive products, Villeroy said.
For the first half of the year, Villeroy reported group pre-tax profits fell to 5.1 million marks from 43.5 million marks in the first half of 1995.
Meanwhile income from ordinary activities dropped 63.1 percent to 20.2 million marks while sales eased 5.8 percent to 718.3 million marks from 762.3 million marks.

At the parent level, Villeroy reported similarly disappointing results saying pre-tax profits slumped 82.7 percent to 5.7 million marks with income from oridary activities retreating 67.2 percent to 12.4 million marks.
Villeroy explained the stronger-than-planned decline in pre-tax profits was largely due to high reserves earmarked for the restructuring and overhaul of a German plant producing sanitary fittings.
The group said it was planning on high extraordinary costs this year, saying these would largely impact the year's results.
Villeroy reduced its workforce by nearly six percent to 10,051 people and plans to cut still more jobs, but a group spokesman declined to say how many more jobs may have to go.
To adjust to market conditions, which Villeroy expects will remain difficult for some time, the group plans to cut costs further after having already introduced lines of less expensive products.
But the spokesman said the group was not planning to go so far and close down any production sites.
Villeroy was much more optimistic for the next year and said it should post satisfactory results in 1998.
Among its individual business areas, bathroom fittings and sanitary equipment posted the biggest loss in sales, falling 15.4 percen to 237.2 million marks.
Tile sales dropped nearly three percent to 255.5 million marks while table settings increased by 3.1 percent to 225.6 million marks.
